_doc: Names that are NEVER stored as a wildlife clip, even when taxa.json calls them a mammal or bird and BirdNET is sure. Read by analysis/clips.py. `names`: whole-name match, case-insensitive, on the detection's scientific OR common name; `prefixes`: match the start of either name (a genus prefix ends in a space). Deliberately conservative: an entry costs at most one missed clip, a missing entry could store a person or a pet. Covers (checked against BirdNET_GLOBAL_6K_V2.4_Labels.txt) farmyard and pet birds (chicken, guineafowl, peafowl, Muscovy duck, Swan Goose, graylag goose, quail, domestic pigeon, canary, zebra finch) and the parrot, cockatoo, macaw, lovebird and myna genera, which are kept as pets and mimic human speech. Groups other than bird, insect, amphibian, mammal and other-bio (taxa.json mechanical) and rows with non_species true are rejected before this list is consulted, so the BirdNET 2.4 non-species classes (Dog, Engine, Environmental, Fireworks, Gun, Human vocal, Human non-vocal, Human whistle, Noise, Power tools, Siren) appear here only as a second line of defence. `human_top_labels` / `human_top_p`: AudioSet labels in a tags row's `top` list that mean a person is present (laughter, crying, screaming, coughing, humming, whistling, crowds, singing ...); a row with one of them at or above human_top_p blocks every clip within the guard span, even when speech_p is low (the tagger's SPEECH_LABELS miss these). `top` holds at most 5 labels with p >= 0.05, so a human label ranked below the top 5 is not seen: speech_p remains the other defence. The rest of the privacy guard (speech flags, human BirdNET labels, tagger availability) does NOT depend on this file.
